topic: The Ternary Bridge: From Hanoi Towers to the Sierpinski Triangle
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Discrete Mathematics)

sections.title: The Base-3 Intuition
lecture_lines: Ternary systems utilize three states: zero, one, two.
Three states naturally represent transitions between three locations.
Base-three counting simplifies Hanoi Tower movement patterns.
animations: Display three disks in a column on the screen.
Fade in three different colors for each disk: #FF5733, #33FF57, #3357FF.
Label disks as Size 0, Size 1, Size 2 near their positions.
Animate shifting the disks to demonstrate base-3 representation.
Highlight the disks with #FFFFFF to finalize the base-3 visual.

sections.title: Constrained Towers of Hanoi
lecture_lines: Disks move only between adjacent pegs in this variation.
Moving three disks requires exactly twenty-six steps.
The move count follows the pattern three to n minus one.
animations: Show initial configuration of Towers of Hanoi.
Display constraint: Move disks to adjacent pegs only.
Visualize the limited move paths with color #FFFF00.

sections.title: Mapping Moves to the Sierpinski Triangle
lecture_lines: Map disk configurations to points on a triangle graph.
Legal moves represent edges between adjacent sub-triangles.
The entire state space forms a Sierpinski triangle.
animations: Display a triangle structure with color #FFFFFF.
Map the recursive move steps to triangle vertices.
Show path tracing through the triangle using #FF00FF.

sections.title: The Synthesis: Recursive Harmony
lecture_lines: Ternary numbers serve as precise path coordinates.
Incrementing ternary values dictates optimal movement sequences.
This recursive harmony guides paths through the fractal.
animations: Overlay triangle structure onto tower state diagram.
Animate recursive moves following the Sierpinski path.
Synthesize final state with color #00FFFF for clarity.
